title: Absolute vs Relative Risk, NNT and NNH

hook.en: "Halves your risk!" sounds wonderful. But halving a risk of 2 in 100 gives 1 in 100, and that may not be worth much. Learn the two ways of describing the same result, and a number that tells you how many patients you must treat for one to benefit.
hook.ur: "Aap ka khatra aadha!" bohat achha lagta hai. Lekin 100 mein 2 ke khatre ko aadha karne se 100 mein 1 hota hai, aur shayad is ki zyada qeemat nahi. Ek hi nateeje ko bayan karne ke do tareeqe seekhein, aur woh number jo batata hai ke ek ko faida dene ke liye kitne mareezon ka ilaaj karna hoga.

goal.en: By the end, you'll calculate absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction and the number needed to treat (NNT) from simple figures, explain the number needed to harm (NNH), and show patients risks in natural frequencies.
goal.ur: End tak aap saade figures se absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction aur number needed to treat (NNT) nikalenge, number needed to harm (NNH) samjhayenge, aur mareezon ko khatre natural frequencies mein dikhayenge.

text.en: **Absolute risk** is how many people in a group get the outcome (for example, 10 in 100). **Absolute risk reduction (ARR)** is the difference between the risk in the control group and the treatment group. **Relative risk reduction (RRR)** is that difference as a fraction of the control risk. **Number needed to treat (NNT)** is 1 divided by ARR: how many people need the treatment for one extra person to benefit. **Number needed to harm (NNH)** is the same idea for side effects. Relative numbers sound bigger; absolute numbers tell you what actually happens.
text.ur: **Absolute risk** ek group mein kitne logon ko nateeja hota hai (masalan 100 mein 10). **Absolute risk reduction (ARR)** control aur ilaaj group ke khatre ka farq hai. **Relative risk reduction (RRR)** woh farq control khatre ke hisse ke taur par hai. **Number needed to treat (NNT)** 1 ko ARR se taqseem karne par milta hai: kitne logon ko ilaaj chahiye taake ek aur ko faida ho. **Number needed to harm (NNH)** side effects ke liye wahi khayal hai. Relative numbers bare lagte hain; absolute numbers batate hain asal mein kya hota hai.

text.en: Think of **a lottery discount**. "Triple your chances of winning!" sounds exciting, but going from 1 in 10 million to 3 in 10 million is still almost nothing. The relative change is large; the absolute change is tiny. Always ask: "three times what?"
text.ur: **Lottery ki riayat** sochein. "Jeetne ke imkaan teen guna!" dilchasp lagta hai, lekin 1 in 1 crore se 3 in 1 crore tak jana phir bhi tareeban kuch nahi. Relative tabdeeli bari hai; absolute tabdeeli bohat chhoti. Hamesha poochhein: "teen guna kis ka?"

rows.ur: 1 / 0.05 = 20 mareezon ka ilaaj taake ek girna rukay

question.en: In a trial, 10 in 100 patients in the control group are re-injured and 5 in 100 in the exercise group. What is the NNT?
question.ur: Trial mein control group ke 100 mein 10 mareez dobara zakhmi hote hain aur exercise group ke 100 mein 5. NNT kya hai?

feedback.en: That is the relative number, not the NNT.
feedback.ur: Yeh relative number hai, NNT nahi.

text.en: 20, because ARR is 5 percentage points and 1 / 0.05 = 20
text.ur: 20, kyunke ARR 5 fisad points hai aur 1 / 0.05 = 20

feedback.en: Yes — twenty patients are treated for one to avoid re-injury.
feedback.ur: Haan — bees mareezon ka ilaaj taake ek dobara zakhmi hone se bache.

feedback.en: RRR is not used that way.
feedback.ur: RRR is tarah istemal nahi hota.

question.en: A press release says "Treatment reduces risk by 40 percent". The risk fell from 5 in 1,000 to 3 in 1,000. How would you describe this to a patient?
question.ur: Press release kehta hai "Ilaaj khatra 40 fisad kam karta hai". Khatra 1,000 mein 5 se 3 hua. Mareez ko kaise bayan karenge?

text.en: "Out of 1,000 people, 5 would have the problem without treatment and 3 with it, so treatment helps 2 in 1,000."
text.ur: "1,000 logon mein se ilaaj ke baghair 5 ko masla hota aur ilaaj se 3 ko, yani ilaaj 1,000 mein 2 ko madad deta hai."

feedback.en: Yes — natural frequencies show the real size.
feedback.ur: Haan — natural frequencies asal size dikhate hain.

text.en: "It prevents almost half of all cases."
text.ur: "Yeh taqreeban aadhe cases ko rokta hai."

feedback.en: It sounds big but applies to a tiny risk.
feedback.ur: Bara lagta hai lekin chhote khatre par lagu hai.

text.ur: "Yeh 40 fisad logon par kaam karta hai."

feedback.ur: Yeh relative figure ko ghalat parhna hai.

question.en: A treatment has an NNT of 10 for pain relief and an NNH of 25 for a side effect. How should you read this?
question.ur: Ilaaj ka dard ke aaram ke liye NNT 10 hai aur side effect ke liye NNH 25. Ise kaise parhein?

text.en: It is harmful, because 25 is bigger than 10
text.ur: Yeh nuqsandeh hai, kyunke 25, 10 se bara hai

feedback.en: A larger NNH means harm is less frequent.
feedback.ur: Bara NNH matlab nuqsan kam aam hai.

text.en: For every 10 treated, one gets benefit, and for every 25 treated one has the side effect, so benefit is more frequent than harm but both must be weighed
text.ur: Har 10 ke ilaaj par ek ko faida, aur har 25 ke ilaaj par ek ko side effect, yani faida nuqsan se zyada aam hai lekin dono ko tolna hoga

feedback.en: Yes — compare NNT and NNH along with severity.
feedback.ur: Haan — NNT aur NNH ka muqabla shiddat ke saath karein.

feedback.en: The numbers help decide, not forbid.
feedback.ur: Numbers faisle mein madad dete hain, mana nahi karte.

text.en: **Quoting only the relative figure.** "Halves the risk" and "doubles the benefit" without the baseline risk are meaningless. Always ask "of what?" and look for the absolute risk. Another trap is treating the NNT as fixed: it depends on the baseline risk, so the same treatment has a lower (better) NNT in high-risk patients than in low-risk ones.
text.ur: **Sirf relative figure quote karna.** "Khatra aadha" aur "faida dugna" baseline khatre ke baghair be-maani hain. Hamesha poochhein "kis ka?" aur absolute khatra dhoondhein. Ek aur jaal NNT ko mustaqil samajhna hai: yeh baseline khatre par munhasir hai, isliye wahi ilaaj zyada khatre wale mareezon mein kam (behtar) NNT rakhta hai.

text.en: **Use natural frequencies with patients.** "If 100 people like you did nothing, about 20 would fall this year. If they all did the programme, about 15 would. So about 5 in 100 are helped." Pictures with 100 stick figures make it clearer still. It respects the patient and avoids hype.
text.ur: **Mareezon ke saath natural frequencies istemal karein.** "Agar aap jaise 100 log kuch na karein to takreeban 20 is saal girenge. Agar sab programme karein to takreeban 15. Yani 100 mein takreeban 5 ko madad milti hai." 100 stick figures wali tasveerein mazeed saaf karti hain. Yeh mareez ki izzat karta hai aur hype se bachata hai.

question.en: Why does the same treatment have a different NNT in different patients?
question.ur: Wahi ilaaj mukhtalif mareezon mein mukhtalif NNT kyun rakhta hai?

answer.en: NNT depends on the baseline risk. If a treatment cuts risk by 25 percent (relative), it helps 5 in 100 when the baseline is 20 percent but only 1 in 100 when the baseline is 4 percent. So a treatment worth giving to high-risk patients may not be worth the cost, effort or side effects in low-risk ones.
answer.ur: NNT baseline khatre par munhasir hai. Agar ilaaj khatra 25 fisad (relative) kam karta hai to jab baseline 20 fisad ho to 100 mein 5 ko madad karta hai lekin jab baseline 4 fisad ho to sirf 100 mein 1 ko. Isliye zyada khatre wale mareezon ko dene ke qabil ilaaj kam khatre walon mein kharch, mehnat ya side effects ke qabil nahi ho sakta.

beats.patient: A trial of a balance programme shows a 30 percent relative reduction in falls. In frail older people, 40 in 100 fall in a year without the programme; in healthy older people, 8 in 100.
beats.assessment: The same 30 percent relative reduction means very different absolute benefits.
beats.treatment: Frail group: ARR = 12 points, NNT about 8. Healthy group: ARR = 2.4 points, NNT about 42. She prioritises the programme for frail patients.
beats.reassess: Limited places are used where they help most, and healthy patients get a lighter option.

text.en: **Weigh benefit against harm.** A small benefit may not justify a serious side effect. Always compare NNT with NNH and consider how bad each outcome is: one prevented fracture is not the same as one extra bruise. Be especially careful with frail patients, who usually have more to lose from harm.
text.ur: **Faide ko nuqsan ke saath tolein.** Chhota faida seriyas side effect ko jaiz nahi thehra sakta. Hamesha NNT ka NNH se muqabla karein aur sochein har nateeja kitna bura hai: ek rokki gayi fracture ek aur nila nishan ke barabar nahi. Kamzor mareezon ke saath khaas ehtiyat karein, jinhein nuqsan se aam taur par zyada khone ko hota hai.

text.en: Laupacis, Sackett and Roberts proposed the number needed to treat as a clinically useful measure of the consequences of treatment, since it directly states how many patients must be treated to prevent one bad outcome. Altman described how to calculate confidence intervals for the NNT, noting that when the benefit is not statistically significant, the interval can include an infinite NNT, which must be reported carefully.
text.ur: Laupacis, Sackett aur Roberts ne number needed to treat ko ilaaj ke nateejon ka clinical taur par mufeed naap tajweez kiya, kyunke yeh seedha batata hai ke ek bura nateeja rokne ke liye kitne mareezon ka ilaaj karna hoga. Altman ne NNT ke confidence intervals nikalne ka tareeqa bayan kiya, aur likha ke jab faida shumariyati taur par significant na ho to interval mein anant NNT shamil ho sakta hai, jise ehtiyat se report karna chahiye.

text.en: **Of what? How many? Who?** Of what baseline risk, how many people (NNT), and in whom does it apply.
text.ur: **Kis ka? Kitne? Kis par?** Kis baseline khatre ka, kitne log (NNT), aur kis par lagu hota hai.

summary.en: Absolute risk reduction shows the real difference; relative risk reduction can sound bigger than it is.
summary.ur: Absolute risk reduction asal farq dikhata hai; relative risk reduction asal se bara lag sakta hai.

summary.en: NNT is 1 divided by ARR, and it depends on the baseline risk.
summary.ur: NNT 1 ko ARR se taqseem hai, aur baseline khatre par munhasir hai.

summary.en: Show patients natural frequencies and weigh NNT against NNH.
summary.ur: Mareezon ko natural frequencies dikhayein aur NNT ko NNH se tolein.

back.en: 1 divided by the absolute risk reduction.
back.ur: 1 ko absolute risk reduction se taqseem.
Control khatra minus ilaaj ka khatra.

front.en: Why is relative risk misleading alone?
front.ur: Akela relative risk gumrah kyun karta hai?

back.en: It ignores the baseline risk and can make small effects sound large.
back.ur: Yeh baseline khatre ko nazar-andaaz karta hai aur chhote asaron ko bara bana sakta hai.

back.en: The number of people treated for one extra person to be harmed.
back.ur: Kitne logon ka ilaaj karne par ek aur ko nuqsan hota hai.
